title: Orchestrated credential profiles and multiplexing pullstream shim
author: Diego Morales
description: Context: Several customers and downstream SDK teams reported jitter and unnecessary reauth churn when a single application multiplexes multiple logical streams over long-lived connections. Motivation: introduce a lightweight orchestrated credential profile model plus a small pullstream adapter that lets SDKs pin a credential profile per logical stream while sharing transport-level heartbeats, reducing reauth noise and improving burst behaviour. This PR implements a cross-language surface and coordinated runtime invariants and ships companion version bumps for the three SDKs. Scope: 1) credential profiles v2 (shape-stable, smaller footprint) implemented in Python/TS/Go SDKs, 2) a PullstreamMultiplexer shim that exposes a typed StreamHandle->Profile mapping for callers and handles on-the-wire multiplexing, 3) a small backoff harmonizer that aligns retry jitter windows across SDKs to avoid thundering reauth storms, and 4) docs + migration guide and unit/integration tests. Design highlights: credential profiles are declarative presets (idle_ttl, reauth_threshold, prewarm hooks) that can be composed; the PullstreamMultiplexer stitches an id-assigned logical stream into a single transport connection while maintaining per-stream credential leases and allows graceful checkpointed resume. Rollout plan: feature-flagged at runtime, staged rollout behind canary config for dedicated customers, with telemetry gates for reauth-rate and connection churn. Backwards compatibility: default profile maps to existing behavior so this is non-breaking for consumers unless they opt-in. Testing: added cross-sdk unit tests, e2e with local multiplexed harness, and a small chaos scenario that simulates credential expiry and prewarm flows. Related: builds on prior session-lease work (ENG-8710) and the credential prefetch RFC (ENG-9302).

review_comments: Aisha Patel (2026-01-13): Nice isolation of profile serialization, can we tighten the JSON schema to reject unknown top-level keys? Suggest adding a validation layer so future changes are explicit.

Diego Morales (2026-01-14): Added a note and a simple sharded reconciler in multiplexer.go behind a build flag; left single-shard default for safety. We can enable after perf tests.

release_notes: Introduce credential profiles v2 and PullstreamMultiplexer shim. Adds non-breaking opt-in API for per-logical-stream credential presets, reduces reauth churn for multiplexed workloads, and harmonizes retry jitter across SDKs. SDK versions bumped: python -> 1.12.0, typescript -> 2.34.0, go -> v1.9.0. See docs/sdk/multiplexing-migration.md for migration steps.
